name: agent-hq
problem: The problem — an AI with no guardrails: it sometimes breaks existing code it was never asked to touch, and hallucinates — inventing functions, libraries, or output that do not actually exist. These rules are the guardrails against that.
rules: Edit surgically: change only the code the task requires — never rewrite a whole file.
Use only libraries that are already in the project. Never invent package names or APIs.
After coding, run the project's validation before saying the task is done: `npm run lint` (lint), `npm run build` (build).
When unsure about existing code, read the surrounding files first before changing anything.

Read memory/INDEX.md before coding — it is the project's local memory (decisions, gotchas, and do-not-touch files). When you need only the notes relevant to a question, run `reviewer-harness context "<question>"` — it walks the memory graph from the best matches and returns just those notes within a token budget, instead of the whole memory. When you learn something new about the project, write it as a note in memory/ with [[links]] to the related notes.

Validate and report every change: after editing any code, run the project's validation (tests, lint, or build), then report every file you changed and show the actual validation output. A change is not done until it has been validated and reported — never finish silently.
goal: Build an "AI office" web app that anyone can use with their own AI APIs: a Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind PWA deployed on Vercel where each user signs up for their own account, connects their own API providers — direct provider APIs such as Gemini API, Groq, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, or Cloudflare Workers AI, or any OpenAI-compatible router endpoint such as FreeLLMAPI or OmniRoute — and gets a personal office showing their own AI team at work. Each agent is assigned to one of the user's APIs, runs real tasks through it from a runner, and usage is tracked per user and per API. The office shows each agent's status and current one-line task, a pending-approvals queue the user can approve or reject from their phone, project activity, runner online/offline with an honest last-seen time, and a peek into the team's shared memory. Every user's office, data, and API keys are isolated by Supabase Auth + Row Level Security: nobody can see another user's office, use another user's API keys, or bypass the login to reach the data. It must never fake live status and never expose one user's data to another. For Edsiel himself, the first providers wired in are his own: FreeLLMAPI (working today) and OmniRoute (supported by the same config; needs revival on his PC first), and his office shows his named harness agents (Bantay, Tigplano, Tig-ayo) and CLI workers via a small Node.js reporter on his PC.
